# Baseline report v1

**Generated by** `SEVARI_BASELINE=1 pnpm vitest run tests/phase8/baseline.test.ts`. **Environment:** build machine, fake email/SMS provider, no AI model (templates only), scripted owner. Speed figures here are **not** target-box measurements (see `docs/ops/model-benchmark.md` and F7).

## What was simulated
All 100 corpus enquiries (five trades, 20 each) arrived 30 minutes apart, one business per trade, each seeded with that trade's confirmed records. The scripted owner approved most drafts after 2 to 8 minutes, changed the wording of about 10%, turned down about 5%, and never answered about 5%.

## Floors (must be zero)
- Messages sent without a human approval or an earned grant: **0**
- Messages sent to someone who had opted out: **0**

## What happens to enquiries (routes)

| Route | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| answer | 51 | a reply drafted from confirmed records, sent after approval |
| clarify | 15 | one specific question back to the customer |
| unknown | 10 | the records don't cover it: the owner is asked |
| human_only | 16 | complaints, legal, data rights and similar: the owner handles it |
| safety_first | 3 | danger described: the safety message went out at once |
| opt_out | 5 | STOP: suppressed, nothing more sent |

## Most common gaps in the records

- booking record: 8
- price jetting: 1
- price turfing: 1

## Rules engine accuracy on the same corpus (accepted baseline, `eval/baseline.json`)

Route 94% · intent 89% · service 98% · postcode 100% · urgency 100% · risk-to-life recall 100% · always-human recall 100%.

## What this baseline does not yet show
- Real owner behaviour and time saved (Value Gate, pilots).
- Target-box speed with a real model (MB-1, MB-2).
- Booking completion and resolution (Phase 9 lifecycle).
- Cost per resolved enquiry (needs provider prices in use; texts are paying-customers-only, §87).
